correctness.rationale: For every d>=3, alternating B and linear L over F3, expansion of the right distributivity cocycle gives 3(Ca+Db)=0. The exact four-variable medial defect is -(B wedge L)(v-u,w-u,z-u). For nonzero three-form and affine-spanning projected seeds, a triple of seed differences has nonzero defect; this produces all central coordinates in one fibre and then all others via the quandle operation. Conversely the projection of a generated subquandle cannot leave the affine span. The all-k counting formula follows from the number of rank-d d-by-(k-1) matrices and 3^k central lifts. The verifier exhaustively checked the 81-point canonical case and 531441 projected quadruples and independently tested the general identities. Finite tests are not treated as a general proof.

originality.rationale: The finite nonmedial order-81 quandle and a four-point medial-law witness are classical and explicitly republished in 2026; they are NOT asserted new. The new theorem uniformly characterizes all generating subsets of every nonzero cubic B-wedge-L central extension in all dimensions and counts every ordered generating k-tuple. Inspected source statements and their mathematical implications do not supply this strong if-and-only-if criterion or the exact rank-matrix probability law. value.rationale: The cubic central-extension family generalizes the historic smallest nonmedial commutative quandle to arbitrary dimensions. The result identifies all generating subsets from a linear-algebraic projection and counts every generating tuple, yielding a parameter-independent random generation law and sharp minimal generator rank d+1. This is a natural structural invariant about recovery of the whole nonmedial operation rather than another example or simple four-variable medial counterexample.
